name: Ford 5.2 L 'Voodoo' V8 (Shelby GT350, 2015-2020)
summary: Flat-plane 90-degree V8 with an unusual up-down-up-down crank and firing order 1-5-4-8-3-7-2-6: banks alternate evenly, giving a hard-edged howl rather than a cross-plane burble, through 4-3-1 headers and an X-pipe.

rod_length_mm.note: Factory length not found on an opened page. A search-result summary showed an aftermarket Manley rod for this engine at 5.933 in centre-to-centre (page blocked); unverified lead.

firing_order.note: Ford numbering: cylinders 1-4 on the right (passenger) bank front to rear, 5-8 on the left. The bank assignment is sourced from Street Muscle's article, which maps the Coyote's Ford-numbered order to R/L and calls 1 and 2 right-bank cylinders. With that numbering this order is R-L-R-L-R-L-R-L.

crank.value: flat-plane (180-degree), throws arranged up-down-up-down front to rear, each pin shared by one cylinder from each bank
crank.note: MotorTrend: Ferrari and most inline fours use up-down-down-up; Ford chose up-down-up-down because it breathed best with a single shared intake plenum. Wikipedia repeats this and says the firing order is unique to the Voodoo as a result.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Even 90 degrees engine-wide with strict right-left alternation, so each bank fires evenly every 180 degrees. Within the right bank the sequence is 1, 4, 3, 2; within the left bank 5, 8, 7, 6 (my reading of the firing order with Ford numbering).

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: 'two 1.51-inch hollow stem intakes'. Magazine article, not a Ford spec sheet.

intake_lift_mm.note: 0.551 in per Ford's release as reported by Enginelabs.

intake_duration_deg.note: Not found on an opened page. A search-result summary reported a forum post quoting 259 degrees intake duration from calibration data, lift basis unstated (not opened).

variable_valve_timing.value: variable cam timing fitted; which cams and what phasing range not stated
variable_valve_timing.note: Street Muscle: 'variable cam timing also plays a part'. Wikipedia mentions VCT mechanisms on the GT350R.

redline_rpm.note: MotorTrend says the valvetrain is designed to survive over-revs to 9,000 rpm.

peak_power_kw.note: 526 hp at 7,500 rpm; converted by me.

peak_torque_nm.note: 429 lb-ft at 4,750 rpm; 90 percent of peak torque from 3,450 to 7,000 rpm.

intake_type.value: single plenum, scroll-type manifold with long large-section runners and charge-motion flaps
intake_type.note: Runners 'as long as those in the 5.0-liter V-8 but much bigger in cross-section'; no dimensions given.

header_type.value: 4-into-3-into-1 per bank, hand TIG-welded tubular manifold
header_type.note: Ford's engineers said 4-2-1 was ideal but packaging around the steering forced 4-3-1.

exhaust_notes.value: banks mix in an X-shaped crossover, then a two-stage muffler with valves that open under load or on demand

missing: cam duration and timing events, phaser range

sources.what: Wikipedia, Ford Modular engine, Voodoo section. Bore, stroke, CR, ratings, redline, firing order, crank layout (citing MotorTrend and Car and Driver).
MotorTrend (Frank Markus, 3 June 2015), technical briefing from Ford's engine team. Crank layout, lift, throttle, manifold and exhaust design.
Street Muscle magazine, 'Inside Ford's New 5.2L Shelby GT350 Engine'. Valve diameters, R/L firing pattern and Ford bank numbering.
EngineLabs report of Ford's final spec release. Bore/stroke in inches, .551 in lift, 87 mm throttle.
WardsAuto interview with chief engineer Eric Ladner. Ratings with Nm, development targets.
f150hub spec table. 32 valves, roller finger followers, max engine speed.

vehicle.name: Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 (2016)

curb_kg.note: '2016 Ford Shelby GT350 Base - Coupe 5.2L V8 Manual ... Curb weight 3,760 lbs.', converted by me. A search-engine excerpt of Ford's tech-spec sheet (https://media.ford.com/content/dam/fordmedia/North%20America/US/2015/08/24/gt350-gt350r-tech-specs.pdf, not read: it returned Access Denied) gives the same 3,760 lb for the GT350 and 3,791 lb with the Track Package.

gear_count.note: Tremec press release quoting Ford: 'the all-new 5.2-liter will be paired with a six-speed manual transmission as its only gearbox option. The TREMEC TR-3160 six-speed manual is specifically engineered for ... the new Shelby Mustangs.'

gears.note: Selected gear ratios table: 'Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 3.25 2.23 1.61 1.24 1.00 0.63 2.95' (reverse last), citing Tremec. Not cross-checked against a Ford document (Ford's PDF refused access). mustangspecs.com's spec table gives different, Mustang GT-like ratios with a 3.55 final drive that contradict its own text; not used.

final_drive.note: 'The power train includes a 3.73:1 ratio, TORSEN helical differential to handle the 5.2 liter's power.'

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from the tyre size (half the rim diameter plus section width times aspect ratio): the unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius; the loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.

tyre.note: '19"x10.5 front wheels and 19"x11 ... rear wheels with 295/35ZR19 front and 305/35ZR19 rear tires. They are Michelin Pilot Super Sport'. Rear-wheel drive.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Shelby Mustang' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: FR layout.

missing: Ford's GT350 tech-spec sheet (refused automated access)

sources.what: Wikipedia, Tremec TR-3160: gear-ratio table with a Shelby GT350 row, citing Tremec.
Tremec press release (June 2015) reproducing Ford's announcement: TR-3160 is the GT350's only gearbox.
MustangSpecs 2016 Shelby GT350 page: text on the 3.73 Torsen axle, wheel and tyre sizes. Enthusiast reference; its spec table is unreliable and not used.
